questions.q: Which alcohol turns Lucas reagent turbid immediately at room temperature?
questions.explain: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol is a 3° alcohol; it forms the stable tert-butyl carbocation fastest and the insoluble chloride separates at once. Propan-2-ol (2°) takes about 5 minutes and the 1° alcohols show no turbidity at room temperature.

questions.q: What is the role of anhydrous ZnCl₂ in Lucas reagent?
options: It absorbs the water formed and so drives the reaction forward
It acts as a Lewis acid that binds the –OH oxygen and makes it a better leaving group
It supplies the chloride ion that acts as the nucleophile
It oxidises the alcohol to a carbonyl compound
questions.explain: ZnCl₂ is a Lewis acid that complexes with an oxygen lone pair, so the activated –OH leaves easily and weakly nucleophilic Cl⁻ can replace it. Calling it merely a water absorber is the common trap.

questions.q: Which primary alcohol gives turbidity with Lucas reagent at once, like a tertiary alcohol?
questions.explain: Benzyl alcohol ionises to a resonance-stabilised benzylic carbocation, so it reacts immediately. A fast Lucas result therefore does not always mean a 3° alcohol.

questions.q: Octan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol, yet the Lucas test is not a reliable way to classify it. Why?
options: It is insoluble in the reagent, so a separate layer forms whether or not it reacts
It reacts by SN2 and gives no chloride
ZnCl₂ dehydrates it completely to an alkene before any chloride forms
Secondary alcohols with more than six carbons are oxidised by conc. HCl
questions.explain: The test relies on a soluble alcohol giving an insoluble chloride; it works only up to about five or six carbons. Larger alcohols form a separate layer anyway, so cloudiness tells nothing.
